claims.claim: A boolean value is one of exactly two values, true or false.
AND (conjunction) is true only when both operands are true; OR (inclusive disjunction) is true when at least one operand is true; NOT (negation) reverses the truth value.
De Morgan's laws state that NOT(A AND B) equals (NOT A) OR (NOT B), and NOT(A OR B) equals (NOT A) AND (NOT B); verified exhaustively over all input combinations.
In Python, 'and' is a short-circuit operator that only evaluates its second argument if the first is true, and 'or' only evaluates its second argument if the first is false.
In Python the boolean operators 'and' and 'or' return one of their operands rather than always returning True or False, and 'not' has lower priority than non-boolean operators.

George Boole introduced an algebraic system for logic, publishing The Mathematical Analysis of Logic (1847) and An Investigation of the Laws of Thought (1854); Augustus De Morgan was a contemporary contributor to the nineteenth-century algebra of logic, and the pair of negation-distribution rules bear his name.
